- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment turns bearish (e.g., <0.00 or -0.33) and price is rising, model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overcorrects downward; apply a 1–3% upward bias to offset mean reversion.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33), model often underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer for early bearish turn.  
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after 10–15 days, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to reflect 2–4 day lag in price drop.  
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is consistently positive but price is falling, model overestimates recovery; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 7–14 days.
